facts.text: In a hypothetical run, context length 2048 uses 7 GB and 8192 uses 11 GB.
Model, runtime and hardware are held fixed.
No output quality or throughput results were collected.

draft.title: Hypothetical Memory Usage: Context Length vs. RAM in Local LLMs
draft.body: I'm exploring the hypothetical memory footprint of local LLMs concerning context length, based on a specific experimental setup. The scenario involves a fixed model, runtime, and hardware configuration (F2). In this hypothetical test, increasing the context length from 2048 to 8192 tokens resulted in a change in RAM usage from 7 GB to 11 GB (F1). It's important to note that no output quality or throughput metrics were collected during this hypothetical exercise (F3). This observation is purely about resource allocation under different context lengths. Does anyone have insights or experience with how RAM scales with context length in similar hypothetical scenarios, keeping other factors constant?
draft.plan: Discuss the hypothetical memory scaling with context length. Keep discussion focused on resource usage, not performance.

draft.title: Hypothetical RAM Scaling with Context Length: Initial Observations
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical experiment focused on memory consumption related to context length in a local LLM setup. The core of this hypothetical is to observe RAM usage changes while keeping the model, runtime, and hardware identical (F2). The preliminary hypothetical data suggests that a context length of 2048 tokens required approximately 7 GB of RAM, whereas increasing this to 8192 tokens hypothetically consumed around 11 GB (F1). Crucially, this hypothetical observation did not involve any evaluation of the model's output quality or processing speed (F3). The objective is to understand the relationship between context window size and memory requirements in a controlled, hypothetical environment. Any thoughts on the implications of this hypothetical RAM scaling for resource planning?
draft.plan: Present hypothetical memory usage data for different context lengths. Emphasize the lack of performance metrics and the hypothetical nature of the findings.
